rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — Verify cash balance against the consolidated balance sheet. Mode B — derive: 12-month claim is the SEC minimum; compute implied runway against the Q1'24 burn rate disclosed in the 10-Q filed 2024-05-03 to test whether management is conservatively or aggressively framing runway.

rfm_tuples.M_value: Cash burn at Q1 2024 run-rate of $109.4M/quarter implies ~$440M annualized burn. $1.51B / $440M = ~3.4 years gross runway, or ~2.5-3.0 years after factoring in $25-35M residual restructuring charges, additional facility-closure costs, and the contingent-consideration liability of ~$35M related to tobevibart/elebsiran milestones. Net of restructuring savings (12% workforce cut completed Q1 2024 + small-molecule discontinuation) burn likely steps down to $90-100M/quarter exiting 2024.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Liquidity claim is conservative — actual cash position supports 2.5-3.5 years operating runway against a Phase 2 readout calendar (HBV MARCH Part B 48-week data Q4'24, SOLSTICE HDV data 2024, HIV VIR-1388 immunogenicity H2'24). Mode B confirms management is not understating runway pressure; the 12-month language is boilerplate not signaling distress. PASS — liquidity is the single strongest positive in the file.

rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — Verify the trial outcome and counterparty termination chronology. Mode B — derive: GSK had a contractual exclusive option to co-develop VIR-2482 after a successful Phase 2; GSK's decision NOT to exercise AND to formally wind down the broader Influenza Program is a third-party validation of the trial readout's severity beyond what management has to disclose.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Item 1 (Note on 2021 GSK Agreement) + Q1'24 10-Q Note 5 (Letter Agreement dated Feb 21, 2024) + 8-K filed 2024-02-22 (accession 0001628280-24-006346)
rfm_tuples.M_value: PENINSULA primary endpoint: protocol-defined ILI was 25/983 (2.54%) placebo vs 24/981 (2.45%) VIR-2482 450mg vs 21/992 (2.12%) VIR-2482 1200mg — i.e. control arm illness rate was so low that the trial was effectively underpowered, and the highest dose showed only a ~16% non-significant reduction. GSK declined the option in the same fiscal year. The Influenza Program was a named pillar of the 2021 GSK Agreement (the deal under which GSK paid $120M for 1.92M VIR shares at $62/share). The 10-K narrative is candid about the trial miss but understates the strategic damage — losing the Influenza Program means GSK has effectively repudiated half of the 2021 collaboration that justified its $120M equity investment at 6-7x current share price. Strong Mode-B negative.

Risk factor explicitly contemplates 'negative revenue' in future periods if GSK reports additional excess-supply charges. Combined with the FDA de-authorization (April 2022), sotrovimab is functionally a runoff asset whose future contribution to revenue is bounded below by zero and may be negative.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The 2022 reported 'net income of $515.8M' was effectively partially clawed back via the 2023 $341.4M payment — and 2022's revenue would be re-cast lower if recognition had been more conservative. Mode B: the 'we are the agent' accounting (Notes 1, 5) means GSK can continue to charge VIR for unused manufacturing capacity into future periods — VIR has explicitly disclosed this could produce NEGATIVE revenue. summary: VIR's FY2023 10-K (filed 2024-02-26) and Q1 2024 10-Q (filed 2024-05-03) document a clinical-stage biotech that has cleanly reverted to its pre-COVID profile after sotrovimab profit-share collapsed -94.7% YoY and the lead post-COVID asset (VIR-2482 influenza mAb) failed Phase 2 in July 2023. The forensic picture is materially distressed at the business-model level — partner GSK has withdrawn from 3 of 4 collaboration scopes (Vaccine Program wound down Feb 2023, Influenza Program wound down Feb 2024, additional-target option lapsed Mar 25, 2024 without exercise) — but disclosure hygiene is clean: Ernst & Young as Big-4 auditor since 2017, unqualified ICFR opinion, no going-concern language, no current material weakness, no litigation, no NT filings. Two restructurings in 5 months and a $300M defensive ATM facility that has not been drawn show contingency-funding posture but not liquidity stress (cash $1.51B + investments yields ~3.4 years runway at current burn). The single asymmetric tail in the file is the sotrovimab profit-share ratchet (Note 1 + Q1'24 10-Q): future periods can be reported as NEGATIVE revenue if GSK charges VIR for additional excess manufacturing capacity — a disclosed but unquantified risk. Pipeline value rests on tobevibart+elebsiran HDV (SOLSTICE Q2 readout, MARCH Part B Q4 2024 readout) and HBV PREVAIL (H1 2025), with management's own DCF inputs assuming 29.1% probability of commercialization. Verdict: NEUTRAL — distressed business model is in plain sight, not obscured; liquidity is strong; honesty-alpha framework EXCLUDES this name from the SHORT bucket because the bad news is fully and forensically disclosed (Phase 2 miss, GSK opt-outs, $341.4M GSK clawback, two restructurings, ATM, CEO sale at depressed price). The same disclosure transparency that creates the bear case also prevents VIR from being a lying-detector SHORT.
